home.onboarding_md:
:material/waving_hand: **New here? Three steps to a live portfolio**

1. **Profile** — add the tickers you follow. You start with ten examples spread across sectors, Europe and crypto; replace them with your own.
2. **Import** — drop a broker statement (Revolut, Trading 212, DEGIRO, Interactive Brokers, ClickTrade or a generic CSV) to fill your transaction ledger; every row is previewed before committing.
3. **Portfolio** — positions, P/L, risk and your tax residence's report then derive from the ledger automatically.

No broker statement? The watchlist below and the **sector screen** work without one — click any ticker for its full analysis page.

home.daily_more_alert_hit: You set this alert on {ticker} {rule} {level}. The price ({price}) crossed it in the latest session and sits {gap} past the level. An alert is your own rule, written in advance: if it was an exit, decide now whether the thesis behind it still holds; if it was an entry, check whether the reason you wanted to buy at that price is still there.
home.daily_more_alert_near: {ticker} trades at {price}, {gap} from your alert {rule} {level}. This is the moment to decide what you will do if it gets there — calmly, before the price decides for you.
home.daily_more_harvest: {ticker} carries a {loss} open loss ({pct}). You have booked {gain} of realised gains this year; selling would offset {offset} of them and lower the base you are taxed on.
home.daily_more_earnings: {ticker} reports {when} ({date}). You hold it: decide beforehand whether you want to go into the print with the whole position, trim it or leave it — after the release, the price will already have moved.
home.daily_more_earnings_watched: {ticker} reports {when} ({date}). You do not hold it: the print is a good moment to check whether it confirms or rules out your case for buying.
home.daily_more_earnings_result: Check whether what changed in the quarter touches the reason you hold or follow it.
home.daily_more_macro_event: {bank} announces its rate decision {when} ({date}). The rate stands at {rate}. A surprise moves growth and indebted companies most, and the currency with them: check how much of your book depends on it.
home.daily_more_macro_result: Higher rates weigh on growth valuations and lower ones relieve them; the currency usually moves with the decision. Check your most rate-sensitive positions.
home.daily_more_rate_history: The previous move was on {date}, from {before} to {rate}.
home.daily_more_tax_year_end: The tax year ends {when} ({end}). You have realised {gain} net so far, and you hold {losses} in open losses and {gains} in open gains. Until then you can still decide what to realise this year: losses offset gains and lower the bill, and gains realised in a year with losses can cost nothing.
home.daily_more_tax_bracket: Your savings base is taxed at {rate} up to {threshold}, and at {next} above it. You have realised {gain} this year, {room} short of the step: if you plan to sell at a gain, splitting the sale across this year and the next can save the difference.
home.daily_more_repurchase_clear: You sold {ticker} on {sold} at a {loss} loss. Buying it back before {date} defers that loss under the repurchase rule; from that date on you can buy again and keep it.
home.daily_more_drawdown: {ticker} is {pct} under your cost ({amount}). It is not a sell order: it is the moment to re-read why you bought it and check whether that is still true. If the thesis is broken the loss already exists; if it holds, the fall may be noise.
home.daily_more_concentration: {ticker} is {weight} of your book. At that weight, one bad quarter from that single company moves the whole portfolio: decide whether it is a deliberate conviction or drift worth trimming.
home.daily_more_low_52w: {ticker} (on your watchlist, not held) trades at {price}, {gap} from its 52-week low. If you had an entry case, this is the price to revisit it at: has something changed at the company, or is it just the market?
home.daily_more_market: An index out of its trend, or carried by few sectors, changes how to read the rest of the card: a fall in your positions may be the market's rather than their own.
home.daily_more_sector_tilt: That bet decides much of how your book behaves against the index.
home.daily_more_vs_benchmark: If the gap comes from one or two positions it is concentrated risk; if it comes from the currency, see the currency line.
home.daily_more_fx: It is the currency's effect, not your companies': nothing to do about it, but worth knowing how much of your return depends on the exchange rate.
home.daily_an_loading: Fetching the comparison and writing the analysis…
home.daily_an_failed: The analysis could not be written right now. Try again in a moment.
home.daily_an_computed: Built from the figures alone — the assistant is not available right now.
home.daily_an_v_behind: {ticker} is {gap} points behind {ref} over three months: the move is largely the company's own, not its group's.
home.daily_an_v_ahead: {ticker} is {gap} points ahead of {ref} over three months: its group is doing worse than the stock itself.
home.daily_an_v_with: {ticker} is only {gap} points away from {ref} over three months: it is moving with its group, so the cause is more the group's than the company's.
home.daily_an_v_mixed: Against {ref}, {ticker} is {m3} points over three months and {y1} over twelve: the two windows disagree, so the recent move is not yet the trend.
home.daily_an_c_self: {ticker}: {m1} in a month, {m3} in three months and {y1} in twelve.
home.daily_an_c_sector: Its sector ({etf}): {m3} and {y1} over the same three and twelve months.
home.daily_an_c_peers: Its peers ({names}): a median of {m3} and {y1}.
home.daily_an_b_growth: analysts expect revenue growth of {value} next year
home.daily_an_b_upside: the mean analyst target sits {value} from the price
home.daily_an_tax: Selling today would realise {loss} against the {gain} gained this year, offsetting {offset}.
home.daily_an_tax_saving: On the savings scale that lowers this year's tax by {saving} — {share} of the amount offset.
home.daily_an_tax_clear: Buying it back before {date} would defer the loss instead.
home.daily_an_hist: In its last {n} prints {ticker} beat the estimate {beats} times, by {surprise} on average, and the stock moved {move} on average between the close before and the close after.
home.daily_an_outlook: For this quarter analysts expect EPS of {eps} ({growth} on a year ago).
home.daily_an_tilt_alt: The sectors that moved least like it over the year: {list}.
home.daily_an_v_tilt_paid: The {sector} bet ({own} of your equity) has paid: over twelve months the sector is {gap} points ahead of the S&P 500.
home.daily_an_v_tilt_cost: The {sector} bet ({own} of your equity) has cost: over twelve months the sector is {gap} points behind the S&P 500.
home.daily_an_attr: Largest drags this month, in points of return: {down}. Largest contributors: {up}.
home.daily_an_v_attr_one: {ticker} alone took {pp} points off the month: the gap is concentrated in one name rather than spread across the book.
home.daily_an_v_attr_spread: No single position explains the gap — the largest drag, {ticker}, took {pp} points: the shortfall is spread across the book.
home.daily_an_market_sectors: Over three months the strongest sectors were {up}; the weakest {down}.
home.daily_an_open_book: Largest open losses: {losses}. Largest open gains: {gains}.
home.daily_an_v_harvest: Selling {ticker} today would lower this year's tax by {saving}; whether to do it is a question about {ticker} itself, which the comparison below answers.
home.daily_an_note_price: Total return in each listing's own currency. Volatility annualised over the last twelve months.
home.daily_an_note_business: P/E and margins: Yahoo Finance. Growth and target: analysts' consensus, not company guidance.
home.daily_an_note_tax: Spain's savings scale, on this year's realised gains alone: other savings income this year changes it.
home.daily_an_note_history: Move: from the close before the report to the close after it.
home.daily_an_note_corr: Correlation of a year of daily returns with the sector you are overweight in: the lower, the more differently it moves.
home.daily_an_note_attribution: Today's weight × the month's move in each listing's own currency: an attribution, not an exact reconciliation.
